title: Siemens and TSMC push AI deeper into chip design - Semiwiki
gist: Siemens and TSMC expanded their EDA collaboration around an AI agent that finds and fixes design-rule violations across Calibre, Aprisa and Solido, plus certifications for TSMC nodes and 3DFabric packaging; the author notes no customer results on time or cost savings were disclosed.

insights.claim: Siemens and TSMC are collaborating on an AI agent that identifies design rule violations, analyzes their context, suggests or carries out fixes, and checks the result, connecting Siemens' Calibre verification with its Aprisa and Solido tools.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: AI-driven sign-off automation could shorten tapeout cycles and strengthen Siemens EDA's position in the TSMC flow.

insights.claim: Design-rule violation fixing is a good fit for AI agents because each violation has a specific context and a result that established software can check, giving the agent a bounded task and a way to test its work.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Suggests agentic EDA will first gain traction on bounded, verifiable tasks.
insights.quote: That gives an AI agent a bounded task and a way to test its work.

insights.claim: Siemens' broader Fuse EDA AI ambition is agents that work through long, multistep tasks across several tools and validate their own outputs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Points to a platform race among EDA vendors for multi-tool agent orchestration.

insights.claim: Design-rule verification is iterative because fixing one violation can create another or affect power, speed or chip area, so it is not a box engineers tick at the end.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Explains why DRC closure is a large time sink and a valuable automation target.
insights.quote: Verification is therefore an iterative part of development, not a box engineers tick at the end.

insights.claim: A passing design-rule check does not prove a change is the best choice for the whole chip, so engineers will still need to judge timing, power and reliability trade-offs.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Limits how much engineering headcount agentic EDA can displace near term.

insights.claim: The Siemens-TSMC announcement describes capabilities and expected benefits but provides no customer results showing how much time or cost the AI tools save.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Investors should discount the productivity claims until measured customer data appears.
insights.quote: does not provide customer results showing how much time or cost they save

insights.claim: Siemens says its tools support several TSMC process technologies and aspects of TSMC's 3DFabric packaging platform, with expanded verification for stacked designs and thermal analysis; some capabilities are certified while others remain under development.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Certification for TSMC flows is a competitive moat in EDA.

insights.claim: Certifying design tools for a foundry's processes and packaging creates an ecosystem effect, letting chip companies use those flows with greater confidence, and Siemens and TSMC are extending training to TSMC design partners.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Reinforces TSMC's ecosystem lock-in and partner EDA vendors' stickiness.

insights.claim: Chip design is becoming as much a coordination problem as a drawing problem, as engineers balance performance, energy, manufacturability, reliability and heat across multiple pieces of silicon.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Raises the value of integrated multi-physics EDA suites.
insights.quote: Chip design is becoming a coordination problem as much as a drawing problem.

insights.claim: The value of the Siemens-TSMC announcement will ultimately depend on measured results: fewer hours resolving violations, faster design cycles, and chips that meet targets when manufactured.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Sets the KPIs to watch for validation of AI-EDA claims.
